subject: Quality checks before furniture leaves the workshop
hook: Two tape measurements tell you if a panel is square.
ig:
Two tape measurements tell you if a panel is square.

Measure corner to corner one way, then the other. Same number both times: square. Different numbers: something's out, and it'll show later as uneven door gaps or a carcass that won't sit flat against the wall.

Why we check it in the workshop:

- An out-of-square panel copies its error into everything built from it
- It's much cheaper to catch at the saw than on site
- It works the same on a single panel or an assembled carcass

Our panels are cut on a sliding table panel saw, and diagonals are part of our check before parts are labelled and wrapped.

Fitters, how often do you check diagonals on bought-in parts? Be honest in the comments.
fb:
A simple trick every joiner knows, and one worth knowing even if you're not one: measure a panel from corner to corner, then across the other way. If the numbers match, it's square.

We check diagonals on panels and carcasses in our Hanley workshop before they go out, because an out-of-square part shows up later as wonky doors and gaps. Have a look at our panel cutting service for the trade.
